data: Stub. The command is being written in go-redfish/redfish and is not in v0.2.0. Nothing below is a promise of a flag name; the reference will be written from the command’s own --help when it is tagged.
data.conventions#Conventions it will follow: A cobra command tree, POSIX flags, --help on every command, output on standard output and errors on standard error. The same safety rules as the library: an https address only, no password in the address, no flag that carries a password (it is read from a file), verification of the BMC’s certificate against --ca-file. Commands grouped as the Ansible modules community.general.redfish_info, redfish_command and redfish_config group them: read, act, configure. The table of which is done is in Parity.
data.reference#Reference: To come, with each command’s flags, exit status and an example, generated from the command itself so that the page cannot drift from the binary.

data.errors#Errors: A refused URL is an ErrInsecure; an HTTP status the BMC answered is a *StatusError. Both can be tested with errors.Is and errors.As.
data.install#Install: go get github.com/go-redfish/redfish@v0.2.0 The module has no dependency outside the standard library.
data.meter#Turn reads into energy:
A Meter turns the successive readings of one BMC into intervals:
var m redfish.Meter // MaxGap 0 means 5 minutes for range time.Tick(time.Minute) { r, err := c.Read(ctx) if err != nil { continue } iv, ok := m.Observe(r) if !ok { continue // the first read is only a baseline } if !iv.Valid { fmt.Println("no energy:", iv.Reason) // never bill 0 as a measurement continue } fmt.Printf("%s %.4f kWh\n", iv.Source, iv.KWh) } With a counter the interval is the counter’s difference, exact even if reads were missed. With only a power it is the trapezoid of two samples, an estimate between them, and samples further apart than MaxGap are not joined. A counter that goes down (a reboot) gives an invalid interval with the reason counter reset, never a negative energy.
data.read#Read a node:
A Client reads one BMC. The address must be https and must carry no credentials; the credentials are given apart, through Credentials, so a password lives as long as a request.
package main import ( "context" "fmt" "log" "time" "github.com/go-redfish/redfish" ) func main() { c, err := redfish.New(redfish.Config{ BaseURL: "https://bmc.example.org", Credentials: redfish.Static{User: "monitor", Password: readSecret()}, Session: true, // log in once, send X-Auth-Token, log out on Close CAFile: "/etc/ssl/bmc-ca.pem", Timeout: 10 * time.Second, }) if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } ctx := context.Background() defer c.Close(ctx) r, err := c.Read(ctx) if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } switch { case r.EnergyKWh != nil: fmt.Printf("%s: %.3f kWh (counter)\n", r.Chassis, *r.EnergyKWh) case r.PowerWatts != nil: fmt.Printf("%s: %.0f W\n", r.Chassis, *r.PowerWatts) } } (readSecret is yours: read the password from a file or a secret store, never from a command line or an environment variable.)
Read takes the EnergykWh counter of the chassis’ EnvironmentMetrics; with no counter, its power (PowerWatts, else the PowerControl of the Power resource). The service is discovered once, from /redfish/v1, and the links it gives are remembered. Config.MetricsPath skips discovery when you know the resource; Config.Chassis picks one chassis out of several.

data: Not released. The mock BMC is being written in go-redfish/redfish and is not in v0.2.0. This page states what it is for; it will be replaced by its reference when it is tagged. Until then, the client’s own tests use a local httptest TLS server.
data.not#What it is not: It is not a model of any vendor’s firmware, and a client that passes against it has shown that it follows the DMTF documents, not that it works on your hardware. Parity with real implementations is a separate question, kept in Parity.
data.serves#What it is meant to serve: the service root, the Chassis, Systems and SessionService collections, with the links a real service gives (so that discovery is exercised); EnvironmentMetrics with an EnergykWh counter, and the older Power resource with its PowerControl, so that both paths of the Meter are tested; sessions (X-Auth-Token) and HTTP Basic authentication over TLS, with a certificate the test can trust through CAFile; faults on demand: a counter that resets, a power with a gap, an oversized answer, a malformed one, a slow one, a redirect: the cases a BMC produces and a unit test would not think of.
data.why#Why a mock: Nothing in a test suite should talk to a real machine: a BMC can power a server off, and a suite that needs one is a suite nobody runs. The mock BMC is a Redfish service in Go that a test starts in-process, or that a developer runs from the command line, so that the client, the command and anything built on them are tested against the protocol rather than against a vendor.

data.method#How parity is judged: The reference is the oracle: a behaviour is ported exactly, then compared with the reference’s answer on the same input, and a difference is either a defect to fix or a documented, deliberate departure. The departures worth knowing already: the client refuses a non-https address and an HTTP redirect, on purpose, whatever the reference accepts.
data.status#Where it stands:
The authoritative table is PARITY.md in the redfish repository, committed with the code it describes, so that a command is marked done in the same change that implements it. This page does not copy it, because a copy is what drifts.
What exists in v0.2.0, and nothing more:
Capability In v0.2.0 service root and discovery yes Basic and session authentication yes energy counter and power reading yes energy from reads (Meter) yes information commands (redfish_info equivalents) not released action commands (redfish_command equivalents) not released configuration commands (redfish_config equivalents) not released mock BMC not released redfish command not released
data.target#The target: The behaviour of the Ansible modules community.general.redfish_info, redfish_command and redfish_config, which are themselves built on the Redfish Specification and the DMTF redfishtool. A Go program that needs a BMC’s answers should not have to shell out to a Python client to get them.

data: A BMC is a privileged network service, often old and rarely patched, and it holds the keys to the machine. The client therefore treats what it says as data to check, and what it is given as secrets to keep short-lived. Every rule below is in github.com/go-redfish/redfish at v0.2.0; the package documentation cites the DMTF text it comes from.
data.bounds#What the client bounds: Size. An answer is read up to MaxBody (1 MiB); a larger one is ErrTooLarge, never an allocation of the size the server announces. Time. Config.Timeout bounds every request, and the contexts you pass cancel them. Shape. A reply that is not the JSON the schema describes is ErrMalformed. Readings that are negative, not finite or absurdly large are discarded by the decoders rather than passed on.
data.fuzzing#Fuzzing and CI: The two JSON decoders (ParseEnvironmentMetrics, ParsePowerConsumed) and the meter are fuzzed, and the inputs that once found a defect are committed under testdata/fuzz/. CI runs go vet, go test -race, a short fuzz run and govulncheck on every change.
data.limits#What it does not do: It does not pin a certificate by fingerprint, only by authority. It does not rate-limit: a caller that polls a BMC every second may exhaust the BMC, which is itself a small computer. A minute is a sensible interval for energy. The mock BMC and the command are not covered by this page until they are released.
data.refuses#What the client refuses: Refused Because Error a URL whose scheme is not https a password travels with every request (Redfish Specification: Basic authentication requires HTTPS) ErrInsecure credentials in the URL a URL ends up in logs, history and error messages ErrInsecure a query or a fragment in the base URL the base is an address, not a request ErrInsecure a MetricsPath outside /redfish/ a configured path must stay inside the service ErrInsecure an HTTP redirect a BMC that sends the client elsewhere would be sent the credentials there the redirect response is returned as an error turning certificate verification off there is no such setting none Certificates are verified against the system roots or, with Config.CAFile, against the authorities in that PEM file (a BMC usually has a private one). TLS 1.2 is the floor.
data.secrets#Secrets:
Credentials is asked for the user and the password when a request needs them, so the caller resolves its secret reference at that moment and the library keeps nothing longer. Error messages are scrubbed of the secrets they could carry. With Config.Session, the password is sent once, to the SessionService; the token is then used, and Close logs the session out.
Keep the password out of command lines and environment variables, where every process of the machine can read it: read it from a file whose mode you check.
